overview.summary: Business operations covering revenue streams, profit strategy, user acquisition, funding rounds, and exit strategies.
overview.marketContext: EdTech market is $150 billion globally, with education sector as a whole worth approximately $6 trillion. Expenditure shifting to non-governmental organizations with focus on US market.

revenue.strategy: Initially free for districts, focus on making money from families and teachers.

streams.name: NFT/Character Sales
streams.description: NFT for cash sales, character and profile customization sales, and swag sales. Items purchasable with coins/points or cash. Some items only purchasable with cash (vanity).

streams.name: Battle Passes
streams.description: Combat profitability through additional battle pass purchases

streams.name: Sponsorships
streams.description: In-game item sponsorships and brand partnerships

streams.name: Transaction Fees
streams.description: Financial transaction fees for paying students for school

fundingRounds.philosophy: Provide as much value as possible, as quickly as possible. Some value costs a lot to create. Need to balance asking amount with getting funded.

rounds.name: Initial Round (Seed)
rounds.goal: Build MVP, start audience, get a testable product into school districts, get feedback, establish university relationships for scholarships

rounds.name: Basic Necessities Round
rounds.description: Ideally grant money, for founder/cofounders and marketing during product development

rounds.name: Basic Necessities Round (Extended)
rounds.description: Same as above with more resources for freelance help

rounds.name: Let's Get Going Round
rounds.description: Proof of concept, testable product, value delivery
team: Full Time Hires (1-2 Software Engineers, 1 Designer)

askingRange.note: The more raised, the faster development and growth

responsibilities: Find businesses looking to improve engagement and work culture

companyCulture.philosophy: Practice what we preach. If gamification works for students, it should work for the team too.

experimentalPM.description: Run the company using the same gamification principles we build for students

concepts.name: Quests Instead of Tasks
concepts.description: Frame work items as quests with clear objectives, XP rewards, and narrative context

concepts.name: XP and Leveling
concepts.description: Team members earn XP for completing work, level up for career progression

concepts.name: Achievement System
concepts.description: Unlock achievements for milestones, innovation, collaboration, and quality

concepts.name: Loot Drops
concepts.description: Random rewards for completing tasks - gift cards, days off, equipment

concepts.name: Guild System
concepts.description: Teams operate as guilds with shared goals and collective rewards

concepts.name: Season System
concepts.description: Quarterly 'seasons' with themes, battle passes, and seasonal rewards

exits.philosophy: Primary goal is to continue growing and scaling the business to be as big as possible, keeping ownership. If acquisition or partnership would help with scaling and providing maximum value to users, it may be an option.

options.name: Gaming Company Acquisition
options.description: Acquisition by a gaming company interested in educational games

options.name: LMS/Large EdTech Company
options.description: Acquisition by learning management system or large educational technology company

options.name: Microsoft/Google/Apple
options.description: Acquisition by major technology company with education initiatives

options.name: Walmart/Amazon
options.description: Acquisition by retail giants with education interests

acquisitions.philosophy: Not a necessity at this time, and probably a bit far out. Prefer building for quality but some things are worth finding or acquiring.

targets.note: Not a fan of the artstyle but could learn from their approach
Open source options likely exist as well

targets.name: Storytailor
targets.note: Hopefully product improves. Also an option for integration. Probably easy to build.

engagement.stakeholderDemand: Teachers, principals, parents, districts all want their students engaged.

currentState.elementaryVsHighSchool: 74% of fifth graders highly engaged vs only one-third of high schoolers

decliningFactors: Overemphasis on grades vs meaningful feedback

attentionSpan.trend: Average attention span decreased from 12 seconds (2000) to 8 seconds (2013)

reducedAttentionCauses.detail: Rapid, fragmented content on TikTok, Snapchat, Instagram overstimulates cognitive processes
16-24 age group engages with multiple screens simultaneously, eroding deep focus capacity
Instant gratification through likes, notifications, endless scrolling trains brain to seek constant novelty
Shorter attention spans linked to poorer test performance, difficulty retaining information

engagement.autonomyEffect: When individuals have freedom to make choices, they feel more motivated and invested, leading to greater creativity, productivity, and satisfaction

keyStats.stat: Engaged students are 2.5x more likely to get excellent grades
Engaged students are 4.5x more likely to be hopeful about the future
47% of students engaged, 29% not engaged, 24% actively disengaged

gamification.overview: The company as a whole is targeting gamification. This is an important topic.

gamingTrends.trend: Younger generations spend more time playing games than ever before

gamification.microsoftExample: Microsoft gives points for searching and playing games, buying up gaming companies - good to learn from their approach
